definition: A campaign whose duration is defined by a fixed or randomly determined number of missions.
A campaign that ends when a participant reaches a specified victory-point threshold.
A campaign that ends after a specified number of real-world time periods rather than a fixed number of battles.
An open-ended campaign with no mandatory final round, usually retaining cumulative standings.
A campaign structure allowing participants to play different numbers of matches concurrently, with scoring adjusted to compensate.
A participant entering a campaign after it has begun, normally receiving defined starting resources or adjusted scoring.
A compensating resource awarded according to the value gap between weaker and stronger campaign forces and spent to modify rolls.
An optional campaign mode in which a defeated unit is temporarily unavailable or loses progress instead of being permanently removed.
abbreviation_or_aliases: non-lethal campaign mode; temporary casualty mode

definition: A bounded family of advancement traits from which a character gains abilities as it levels.
A campaign action that permanently removes a unit from the roster, normally forfeiting its accumulated experience and upgrades.
The maximum permitted spacing between component bases that must remain mutually connected as a unit.
The contiguous area occupied by a formation and the permitted spacing around and between its component elements.
mechanical_role: Defines the spatial footprint within which attached or supporting elements operate

definition: A component base separated beyond permitted formation spacing and unable to move normally until contact is restored.
A proximity distance within which friendly formations or units provide specified mutual support effects.
Damage applied to an abstract headquarters element that degrades the performance of subordinate formations rather than directly removing combat troops.
A command-doctrine rating representing broad local discretion and improving a formation's ability to act under changing conditions.
A command-doctrine rating representing restricted local initiative and making formations less responsive to unexpected conditions.
A movement-state threshold where a model may have physically moved but is still treated as stationary for specified combat effects.
mechanical_role: Separates token movement from mechanically significant movement

definition: A limited ammunition type carried alongside a primary weapon load and capable of becoming exhausted independently.
mechanical_role: Tracks depletion of specialist ammunition without tracking every shot

definition: Fire resolved against an enemy while that enemy is conducting movement rather than during the firer's normal fire opportunity.
mechanical_role: Reaction attack triggered by enemy movement

definition: A temporary interruption in battle tempo that can cancel or curtail normal turn activity and trigger other scenario effects.
mechanical_role: Introduces uncertain pauses into turn tempo

definition: An ordered pipeline of requested indirect-fire missions that arrive after delay as capacity becomes available.
mechanical_role: Models communications and artillery response delay

definition: Moving a crew-served gun or mortar without motorised transport.
mechanical_role: Movement mode for heavy weapons without transport
